role: Three LLM fact namespaces: routes.library.* (count/list saved routes, rename, save a recent GPS workout as a route, engage a saved route as turn-by-turn), app.now.* (UTC time, local date, timezone, weekday) and app.devices.* (Polar, foot pod/FTMS, Concept2 PM5, Zwift BLE broadcaster state).
types: RoutesLibraryNamespace: struct (FactNamespaceResolver, namespace 'routes', holds SessionArchive) — route library facts/actions
AppDevicesNamespace: struct (FactNamespaceResolver, namespace 'app') — connected hardware facts
toplevel: Each namespace is registered by AppFactResolverFactory.registerAppNamespaces (AppFactResolver.swift:214-216). Stored lets: namespace strings and RoutesLibraryNamespace.archive.

units.does: Validates name, picks candidate workouts (date or 20 most recent), takes the first with a GPS polyline, appends it to SavedRouteStore and returns the saved-route record.

flags.text: SavedRouteStore.add/rename mutate the in-memory list then call save(), which silently skips the disk write when the earlier load failed (loadFailed, SavedRoute.swift:322-327). The action still returns status 'saved'/'renamed', so the model confirms a change that is lost on next launch.

Description says without a date it saves 'the most recent workout that has a GPS polyline', but only the 20 newest workouts are searched (prefix(20)); if those are all indoor the action reports no polyline although an older GPS workout exists.

docs/VOICE_AND_TOOL_USE.md says that without a date save_workout defaults to the most recent finished workout and errors when that workout has no GPS polyline; the code skips non-GPS workouts and saves the newest of the 20 most recent that has a polyline.

There is no duplicate check: saving the same workout again appends a second SavedRoute (new UUID) with the same name, after which routes.library.rename and routes.library.engage refuse that name as ambiguous.

flags.text: SavedRouteStepBuilder.build returns nil for a structurally invalid route (<2 trackpoints) as well as on the 3 s timeout, and both get 'still building … ask again in a few seconds; the cache will be warm', so for an invalid route the model keeps telling the user to retry a build that can never succeed.

flags.text: The Polar guards test only whether RRCollector.current has a PolarManager, not whether a strap is connected. With the app running and no strap, recording_hours_since_charge returns the manager's stale hoursRecordedSinceBatteryChanged (0 or the last strap's value) instead of 'no Polar connected', and battery_percent/firmware answer 'battery never reported'/'firmware not yet read' (they are nilled on disconnect, StrapLinkCoordinator.swift:226-228).

flags.text: The Polar guards test only whether RRCollector.current has a PolarManager, not whether a strap is connected. With the app running and no strap, recording_hours_since_charge returns the manager's stale hoursRecordedSinceBatteryChanged (0 or the last strap's value) instead of 'no Polar connected', and battery_percent/firmware answer 'battery never reported'/'firmware not yet read' (they are nilled on disconnect, StrapLinkCoordinator.swift:226-228).

recording_hours_since_charge and spec_capacity_hours are described (and documented) as the 'honest battery-time-left' pair, but hoursRecordedSinceBatteryChanged resets to 0 whenever the strap reports any NEW battery level (for example 80% to 79%), not on a full charge. spec_capacity_hours minus this value therefore overstates remaining battery, and the model gives the user a wrong runtime estimate.
